title: Florida cops say they don't know who owns 11 unpermitted Flock cameras
gist: While removing Flock license-plate cameras under a mandate, St. Lucie County, Florida found 14 unpermitted cameras. Eleven had no known owner and three turned out to belong to the Sheriff's Office. The article puts this alongside a pattern of Flock installing cameras without permits (Cambridge, Millcreek, Palm Bay) and at least 50 US cases of police misusing Flock data. Flock faces growing backlash and removal demands across Florida, the only state to ban the cameras on state roads.

insights.claim: Of 14 unpermitted license-plate cameras found in St. Lucie County, Florida during a mandated Flock removal, 11 had no obvious owner, and the county Sheriff's Office claimed three without explaining why it never obtained permits.

insights.so_what: Weak governance over who installs and accesses ALPR cameras increases regulatory and reputational risk for the surveillance industry.
